C-WINDOWS-TITLEBAR-ALIGNMENT.Name: Windows titlebar platform alignment: native Segoe caption glyphs, amendment-5 bar clusters, honest right-zone clearances
C-WINDOWS-TITLEBAR-ALIGNMENT.Summary: Align the Win/Linux custom titlebar with the platform in the owner-final amended state (five amendment rounds, pixel-verified through eight polygon rebuilds; the full decision chain is the ApprovalBasis): caption buttons render the native Segoe MDL2/Fluent code points (E921/E922/E923/E8BB) with no cell separators and one neutral hover; the app-menu ☰ and Settings ⚙ buttons stay on the Win/Linux bar (palette-only reachability proved undiscoverable — amendment 5); the «?» guide button is removed on every platform (Help › Mark Guide in the window menu bar covers it); the theme toggle rides the caption row as a flush fourth 46 px cell (strip 184 px); and the 30 themes drop the legacy caption-svg fill rule that painted the theme icon as a white dot. macOS keeps its minimal bar (native menu owns menu/settings) minus the removed guide button.
C-WINDOWS-TITLEBAR-ALIGNMENT.ApprovalBasis: Amendment (owner, 2026-10-20, after the pixel-verified build): the hand-drawn caption approximation still reads as non-native — on Windows the caption glyphs now render the SAME system Segoe MDL2/Fluent code points native caption buttons draw (E921/E922/E923/E8BB, 10 px) with the redrawn chrome-icon descriptors kept as the non-Windows fallback.Owner review of the 2026-10-20 Windows polygon (laptop-kari) evidence crops (titlebar, right-zone and center-zoom captures): the owner confirmed all three findings ("very strange" caption buttons, toolbar mismatch with options left on the plate, right-side overhang) and chose: option 1 for the bar (remove ☰ and ⚙, keep «?»), Windows-style rendering for the caption glyphs (bigger/flatter, separators, neutral hover), and the right-zone spacing/plate-clearance repair. Recorded in chat on 2026-10-20 after the code-grounded discussion. Amendment 2 (owner, same day): the caption cell separators are removed — native Win10/11 caption buttons have none; hover-only separation, as native. Amendment 3 (owner, same day): the «?» guide button is removed on every platform (Help › Mark Guide in the window menu bar covers it) and the theme toggle rides the caption row as a flush 4th 46px cell (strip 184px); macOS keeps theme in the right cluster. Amendment 4: the legacy theme rule ".title-bar .frameless-titlebar-button > div > svg { fill: … }" (window-controls.js era) is removed from all 30 theme files — it filled the theme icon solid once it entered the caption cell. Amendment 5 (owner, same day): the ☰ app-menu button and ⚙ Settings gear RETURN to the Win/Linux bar — a day of real use showed the palette-only reachability is undiscoverable; macOS keeps the minimal bar. Everything else stands (Segoe captions, no separators, theme as the 4th cell, no «?»).
C-WINDOWS-TITLEBAR-ALIGNMENT.ProblemEvidence: Polygon screenshots show 10px round-cap hairline glyphs floating in invisible 46px cells (frameless-titlebar-button CSS: transparent at rest, macOS hover rgb(228,79,79) on close); the Win bar carried the pre-C-40 layout ([☰][sidebar][⚙] … [?][theme][share]) while macOS was trimmed in C-40 T-002 to [sidebar] … [title] … [theme,share]; .title-bar.frameless:not(.isOsx) .titlebar-right reserved margin-right:146px against the 138px caption strip (8px gap) and the 420px .titlebar-title-btn plate had no ellipsis guard, so narrow windows crowded the right zone. The intermediate rounds additionally proved: hand-drawn caption glyphs never read as native (fixed by the Segoe code points), visible separators contradicted the platform (removed), palette-only Settings reachability failed the owner's real-use discoverability bar (☰/⚙ restored), and the theme icon entering the caption cell exposed a legacy 30-theme fill rule that painted it as a solid white dot (found via CDP on the live polygon app; rule removed).

Goals.Goal: Caption buttons read as platform-native on Windows: minimize/maximize/restore/close render the system Segoe MDL2/Fluent code points (E921/E922/E923/E8BB) through a .caption-glyph span, with no cell separators and the shared neutral floatHoverColor hover on all cells; the redrawn chrome-icon window-* descriptors (butt caps, full-width geometry on the frozen 16-grid/1.4-stroke set) stay as the non-Windows fallback at 13 px.

The Win/Linux bar keeps its primary entry points per amendment 5 — [☰][sidebar][⚙] … [title plate] … [share] + [theme][min][max][close] caption row — with the «?» guide button removed everywhere and the theme toggle as the flush fourth 46 px caption cell (strip 184 px); macOS keeps the minimal bar (native menu owns menu/settings, theme beside Share) and also loses the guide button.

The 30 themes drop the legacy ".title-bar .frameless-titlebar-button > div > svg { fill: … }" rule so the caption-row theme icon renders as the designed ring+half instead of a solid disc; the title plate keeps ellipsis overflow so long names clip instead of colliding with the right zone.

Constraints.Constraint: Do not touch the shared CHROME_ICON_STROKE (1.4), the 16-grid viewBox, or the CHROME_ICONS name set — chrome-icons.test.js pins them and the whole chrome family shares them; only the four window-* descriptors' geometry changes, and the Segoe code points are private-use glyphs from the system font, not new descriptors.
The Segoe caption path is Windows-only: Linux keeps the drawn SVG fallback (pinned by tests), and macOS rendering changes only by the global guide-button removal.

mt::window-popup-app-menu and OPEN_SETTING_WINDOW keep their bar handlers (amendment 5 restores handleMenuClick/handleSettingsClick and the showCustomTitleBar computed); the command-palette routes remain as redundant reachability.
The C-38 N1 gear pin history stays documented in the tests: amendment 1 superseded it, amendment 5 restored it behind the documented amendment trail — the assertion cites both.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No native-frame return (decorations stay false per tauri.windows.conf.json / C-15 T-W1).
No removal of primary entry points for discoverability's sake (amendment 5): menu and Settings stay on the bar; hidden palette-only replacements failed the owner's live-use check.
No sidebar/status-bar redesign, no mica work (Win10 has none; mica stays Win11-only m058).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: titleBar-windows tests pin: the Segoe code points E921/E922/E8BB on win32 with no svg caption glyphs, the Linux fallback (svg present, no caption-glyph), ☰ and ⚙ restored with their handlers, no «?» anywhere, the theme toggle as the flush fourth caption cell, and no caption cell separators.

chrome-icons tests stay green unchanged except any descriptor-path snapshot: names, frozen set, 1.4 stroke, 16-grid and currentColor all keep holding; the round-cap invariant keeps its documented FLAT_CAP exemption for the four caption glyphs.
The macOS variant (titleBar-osx and the isOsx paths) passes with the guide button removed and theme/share clustering intact.

Polygon visual proof: the rebuilt NSIS shows the Segoe glyphs (pixel-measured against the native Explorer reference), no separators, ☰/⚙ present, no «?», the theme icon as a ring+half in its caption cell, before/after crops per the bundle evidence.

AffectedAreas.Area: src/renderer/src/components/icons/chromeIcons.js (four window-* descriptors + CHANGE_SUMMARY); src/renderer/src/components/titleBar/index.vue (Segoe caption path, amendment-5 clusters, theme caption cell, guide-button removal, CSS + CHANGE_SUMMARY); src/renderer/src/assets/themes/*.theme.css (30 files: legacy caption-svg fill rule removed); tests/renderer/components/titleBar-*.test.js + chrome-icons.test.js (amendment-5 pins); .grace/graph/runtime.xml M-011 summary; .grace/verification/runtime.xml V-M-011 scenario-74; docs/release-trains/2.6.x-next.md FIX-014.

VerificationIntent.Command: Windows polygon: local NSIS rebuild (V-M-046 local-bundle mode) + silent reinstall + cua crops of the amended bar
